name: wireguard-mesh-ws-tunnel
description: WireGuard-over-TCP/443 fallback for hostile networks (airport / hotel / corporate guest Wi-Fi blocking UDP). Sibling to bb-net_wireguard-mesh (the panel) — this folder owns the wstunnel-server that terminates WSS on gcp-proxy and forwards UDP to the kernel WG listener at 127.0.0.1:51820. UDP/51820 remains the primary transport; this kicks in only when clients can't reach UDP.

transports._doc: Canonical declaration of all VPN transport paths. Read by bb-net_wireguard-mesh (the panel) + unix/.../wireguard-wstunnel.nix (the laptop client) + cloud Caddy deriver. Single source of truth — never duplicate these values anywhere.

wg0.label: WireGuard direct (UDP)
wg0.use_case: Default high-speed path. UDP-friendly networks (cloud-to-cloud, home, most cellular).
wg0._consumer_hint: Read by home-manager wireguard.nix on every VM and laptop.

wg0-tcp.label: WireGuard via wstunnel (TCP/443)
wg0-tcp.use_case: Hostile networks (airport / hotel / captive portal) where UDP/51820 is blocked. Looks identical to normal HTTPS to MITM/DPI.
wg0-tcp._consumer_hint: Read by home-manager wireguard-wstunnel.nix on laptop/phone only.

primary._doc: auth=none required: wstunnel client cannot do 2FA cookies. Scanner defence is enforced by the wstunnel server itself via --http-upgrade-path-prefix ${WSTUNNEL_PATH_PREFIX} — Caddy passes WebSocket upgrades through natively (Caddy v2 reverse_proxy handles WS by default).

secrets._doc: WSTUNNEL_PATH_PREFIX (32-char hex) — random secret embedded in the WS upgrade URL path. Required for both server (--http-upgrade-path-prefix) and laptop client (--http-upgrade-path-prefix). Generated by build.sh secrets on first deploy and persisted in sops-encrypted secrets.yaml.
